The Max Planck Institute for Informatics is a non-profit research institute in Saarbrucken, Germany, described in its own materials as a university-affiliated lab. Its stated goal is to advance foundational research and drive innovation in key areas of computer science. The institute says its work spans from the fundamental principles of algorithms and logic to systems such as the Internet, and to multimodal areas including computer vision, computer graphics, databases and information systems, machine learning and artificial intelligence. It describes itself as committed to the advancement of science through people, publications, software, and data.

The institute is part of the Saarland Informatics Campus, which it describes as one of the leading locations for computer science in Germany and Europe. According to the site, that campus brings together four research institutes, the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), the Max Planck Institute for Informatics, the Max Planck Institute for Software Systems, and the Center for Bioinformatics, along with Saarland University and its three departments in Computer Science, Mathematics, and Language Science and Technology.

On the AI side, the site states that in 2022 the Max Planck Institute for Informatics and Google established a strategic research partnership, the Saarbrucken Research Center for Visual Computing, Interaction and Artificial Intelligence (VIA), based at the institute. The center investigates basic frontier research challenges in computer graphics, computer vision, and human machine interaction, at the intersection with artificial intelligence and machine learning. The institute is also tracked under the alias Max Planck. No litigation, commercial products, or other registry entries are recorded for it.
